Are sleep spindles related to schizotypal personality traits and thalamic glutamine/glutamate in healthy subjects?

Please research this question using your tools. You MUST conclude your final response with exactly one of the following lines: 'FINAL DECISION: YES', 'FINAL DECISION: NO', or 'FINAL DECISION: MAYBE'.

Yes. One direct human study found that spindle density was inversely correlated with schizotypal magical ideation (r = −0.64, P < .01) and thalamic Glx (r = −0.70, P < .005). Glx was not significantly correlated with magical ideation (r = 0.12, P > .1).

The study included 20 healthy young men, assessed with two nights of 128-channel EEG and automated spindle detection, thalamic magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and the Magical Ideation Scale. The evidence is limited to this small, all-male sample; detailed results were available from the abstract.

**Citation:** *Sleep spindles are related to schizotypal personality traits and thalamic glutamine/glutamate in healthy subjects.* *Schizophrenia Bulletin* (2015). PMID: [25074975](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25074975/); DOI: [10.1093/schbul/sbu105](https://doi.org/10.1093/schbul/sbu105).

**Yes.** A study of 20 healthy young men found that sleep-spindle density was inversely associated with magical-ideation schizotypy (r = −0.64, P < .01) and thalamic glutamine/glutamate (Glx; r = −0.70, P < .005). However, Glx itself was not significantly associated with magical ideation (r = 0.12, P > .1). These are correlations, not evidence of causation, and the findings are limited by the small, all-male sample.

**Reference:** *Sleep spindles are related to schizotypal personality traits and thalamic glutamine/glutamate in healthy subjects.* *Schizophrenia Bulletin* (2015). PMID: [25074975](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25074975/); DOI: [10.1093/schbul/sbu105](https://doi.org/10.1093/schbul/sbu105).
